subject: Genetics
title: FOXP2 and Language
description: A fast breakdown of FOXP2 and Language for builders.

hook.text: A British family couldn't form words properly. Scientists traced the problem to one gene: FOXP2.

buildup.text: FOXP2 helps coordinate the fine muscle movements needed for speech. Mutate it, and language production breaks down.

discovery.text: Humans have a unique version of FOXP2 with two amino acid changes that appeared about 200,000 years ago.

twist.text: Neanderthals had the same two changes. They may have had language too. We aren't as unique as we thought.

climax.text: FOXP2 isn't the 'language gene'—many genes contribute. But it showed genetics could illuminate our deepest traits.

punchline.text: Two amino acids may have helped humans learn to speak.
